title: The rigged coin
topic: how to make an unfair coin fair
hook: Two rivals. One prize. And one coin to decide who gets it.

cast.description: The younger rival, sharp and suspicious; he spots the trick and finds the fix.
The older rival, confident; he would win with the rigged coin.
The old man who holds the coin and decides by flipping it.

promise: A biased coin becomes fair when you flip it twice and only count heads-tails or tails-heads.

takeaway.text: Flip twice. Heads-tails, the first wins. Tails-heads, the second. Same, flip again.

scenes.narration: Two rivals. One prize. And one coin to decide who gets it.
scenes.visualIdea: The old man holds up the coin, it spins in the air.
scenes.action: The old man shows the coin.

scenes.narration: The old man tosses it in the air. Heads, the first one wins. Tails, the second.
scenes.visualIdea: All three: the old man flips the coin between the two rivals.
scenes.action: The protagonist watches the coin closely.

scenes.narration: But this coin is not fair. It lands heads eight times out of ten.
scenes.visualIdea: A balance scale tips to one side; a sign says eight out of ten.

scenes.narration: The first rival smiles. The second one sees the trick, and he is angry.
scenes.visualIdea: The older rival celebrates, the protagonist argues, the old man shrugs.

scenes.narration: Here is the surprise. You can make a rigged coin fair. Just flip it twice.
scenes.visualIdea: Close on the protagonist: he thinks, then gets the idea; the coin flips twice.

scenes.narration: Heads then tails, the first one wins. Tails then heads, the second. Same odds for both.
scenes.visualIdea: The balance scale comes back level; a sign says fifty fifty.
